at gange.explanation: "At gange" means "to multiply": Jeg ganger to med tre (I multiply two by three). It comes from gange (times): Tre gange to er seks (Three times two is six).

sentence.da: I skolen lærer vi at **gange** og dividere.
sentence.en: At school we learn to multiply and divide.

at gemme.explanation: "At gemme" means "to save", like a file or something you keep for later: Jeg gemmer filen (I am saving the file). It can also mean "to hide": Hun gemte nøglen (She hid the key).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **gemme** billedet på min telefon.
sentence.en: I want to save the picture on my phone.

at gemme sig.explanation: "At gemme sig" means "to hide": Børnene gemmer sig bag sofaen (The kids hide behind the sofa). To hide an object, use at gemme without sig: Jeg gemmer nøglen (I hide the key).

sentence.da: Katten plejer at **gemme sig** under sengen.
sentence.en: The cat usually hides under the bed.

at genbruge.explanation: "At genbruge" means "to recycle" or "to reuse": Vi genbruger flasker (We recycle bottles). Gen- means "again", so it is bruge (to use) again.

sentence.da: Papir og glas kan man **genbruge**.
sentence.en: Paper and glass can be recycled.

at genere.explanation: "At genere" means "to bother", when something or someone is unpleasant or in your way. It is often used politely: Generer jeg dig? (Am I bothering you?)

sentence.da: Musikken kan **genere** naboerne om natten.
sentence.en: The music can bother the neighbors at night.

at genkende.explanation: "At genkende" means "to recognize", when you know someone or something from before: Jeg genkender din stemme (I recognize your voice). It is built from gen (again) and kende (to know), and gen is also in at genbruge (to reuse).

sentence.da: Kan du **genkende** manden på billedet?
sentence.en: Can you recognize the man in the picture?

at gentage.explanation: "At gentage" means "to repeat", to say or do something again: Jeg gentager mit spørgsmål (I repeat my question). It also works for events: Historien gentager sig (History repeats itself).

sentence.da: Kan du **gentage** det langsomt, tak?
sentence.en: Can you repeat that slowly, please?

at gide.explanation: "At gide" means "to be bothered to", and it is about having the energy or will. It is mostly used with ikke or in questions: Jeg gider ikke (I can't be bothered). Gider du komme med? (Do you feel like coming along?)

sentence.da: Han vil nok ikke **gide** at hjælpe os.
sentence.en: He probably won't feel like helping us.

at gifte sig.explanation: "At gifte sig" means "to get married". The little word sig changes to match who is marrying: du gifter dig (you get married), han gifter sig (he gets married). Gift on its own means "married": Jeg er gift (I am married).

sentence.da: De vil **gifte sig** i kirken.
sentence.en: They want to get married in the church.

at give.explanation: "At give" means "to give": Jeg giver dig bogen (I give you the book). It is part of many phrases, such as at give op (to give up) and at give besked (to let someone know).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **give** dig en gave.
sentence.en: I want to give you a present.

at give besked.explanation: "At give besked" means "to let someone know": Giv mig besked i morgen (Let me know tomorrow). To be the one who hears it, use at få besked (to be notified).

sentence.da: Kan du **give besked**, når du er fremme?
sentence.en: Can you let me know when you arrive?

at give en hånd med.explanation: "At give en hånd med" means "to give a hand", or "to help out": Kan du give en hånd med? (Can you lend a hand?) Literally it is "to give a hand along": med (along) means you join in on a job that someone is already doing.

forms.da: jeg har givet en hånd med

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **give en hånd med** flytningen.
sentence.en: We would like to give a hand with the move.

at give lov.explanation: "At give lov" means "to give permission": Min mor gav mig lov (My mom gave me permission). Lov on its own also means "law", but in this phrase it is permission.

sentence.da: Far vil nok **give lov**, når vi spørger pænt.
sentence.en: Dad will probably give permission when we ask nicely.

at give op.explanation: "At give op" means "to give up", when you stop trying: Jeg giver ikke op (I am not giving up). Op (up) is a small word that changes the verb in many phrases: at skrive op (to write down), at ringe op (to call up).

sentence.da: Det er svært, men jeg vil ikke **give op**.
sentence.en: It is hard, but I won't give up.

at give tilbage.explanation: "At give tilbage" means "to give back": Han gav mig pengene tilbage (He gave me the money back). To take something back to a shop or library, use at returnere (to return).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **give tilbage**, hvad jeg har lånt.
sentence.en: I want to give back what I borrowed.

at glemme.explanation: "At glemme" means "to forget", both facts and things you were meant to bring or do: Jeg glemte at ringe (I forgot to call).

sentence.da: Jeg må ikke **glemme** min paraply.
sentence.en: I must not forget my umbrella.

at glæde sig over.explanation: "At glæde sig over" means "to be happy about" something that is here now: Jeg glæder mig over gaven (I am happy about the gift). For the future, use at glæde sig til (to look forward to): Jeg glæder mig til ferien (I look forward to the vacation).

sentence.da: Hun kan **glæde sig over** de små ting i livet.
sentence.en: She can be happy about the small things in life.

at glæde sig til.explanation: "At glæde sig til" means "to look forward to": Jeg glæder mig til weekenden (I look forward to the weekend). Sig changes with the person: Vi glæder os til festen (We look forward to the party).

sentence.da: Børnene begynder at **glæde sig til** sommerferien.
sentence.en: The children are starting to look forward to the summer vacation.

at godtage.explanation: "At godtage" means "to accept" something, like an explanation, an offer or a rule: Jeg kan ikke godtage forklaringen (I cannot accept the explanation). It sounds fairly formal; in everyday speech at acceptere (to accept) is the more usual word.

sentence.da: Vi kan ikke **godtage** den høje pris.
sentence.en: We cannot accept the high price.

at google.explanation: "At google" means "to google", to search for something online: Jeg googler åbningstiderne (I google the opening hours).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **google** en opskrift på pandekager.
sentence.en: I want to google a recipe for pancakes.

at grave.explanation: "At grave" means "to dig", making a hole in the ground: Hunden graver i haven (The dog is digging in the garden). With op (up) it means digging something out: grave noget op (dig something up).

sentence.da: Med en spade kan man **grave** et dybt hul.
sentence.en: With a spade you can dig a deep hole.

at gribe.explanation: "At gribe" means "to grab" and "to catch" something that is thrown: Hun greb bolden (She caught the ball). Han greb min arm (He grabbed my arm).

sentence.da: Kan du **gribe** bolden, når jeg kaster den?
sentence.en: Can you catch the ball when I throw it?

at grine.explanation: "At grine" means "to laugh", usually out loud at something funny: Vi grinede meget (We laughed a lot). Be careful with grine af (to laugh at someone), which can mean mocking them: Hvorfor griner du af mig? (Why are you laughing at me?)

sentence.da: Børnene vil **grine** af den sjove klovn.
sentence.en: The children want to laugh at the funny clown.

at græde.explanation: "At græde" means "to cry", shedding tears from sadness, pain or even joy: Hvorfor græder du? (Why are you crying?)

sentence.da: Barnet er ked af det og vil **græde**.
sentence.en: The child is sad and wants to cry.

at gå.explanation: "At gå" means "to go on foot", so to walk, and also "to leave": Jeg går nu (I am leaving now). It also describes how things are going (Det går godt means "It is going well") and buses and trains that run (Bussen går hver time means "The bus runs every hour"). For going by car or plane, use at køre (to drive) or at flyve (to fly) instead.

sentence.da: Vi vil hellere **gå** end køre.
sentence.en: We would rather walk than drive.

at gå en tur.explanation: "At gå en tur" means "to go for a walk", just for pleasure or fresh air. You can add where: gå en tur i parken (go for a walk in the park). En tur can also mean "a trip", as in en tur til Aarhus (a trip to Aarhus), so the situation tells you which is meant.

forms.en: I have been for a walk

sentence.da: Efter maden vil vi **gå en tur**.
sentence.en: After the meal we want to go for a walk.

at gå forbi.explanation: "At gå forbi" means "to pass by" on foot: Jeg går forbi skolen hver dag (I walk past the school every day). Forbi (past) works with other verbs too: køre forbi (drive past).

sentence.da: Jeg plejer at **gå forbi** bageren på vej hjem.
sentence.en: I usually pass the bakery on the way home.

at gå fra hinanden.explanation: "At gå fra hinanden" means "to break up", literally "to go from each other". It is used when two people end a relationship together: Vi gik fra hinanden i går (We broke up yesterday).

sentence.da: Efter tre år vil de **gå fra hinanden**.
sentence.en: After three years they want to break up.

at gå galt.explanation: "At gå galt" means "to go wrong" and is about plans and events: Alt gik galt i går (Everything went wrong yesterday). For a wrong answer, use forkert (wrong) instead.

sentence.da: Det kan **gå galt**, når vejen er glat.
sentence.en: It can go wrong when the road is slippery.

at gå glip af.explanation: "At gå glip af" means "to miss out on" something you wanted to be part of: Jeg gik glip af festen (I missed out on the party). For a bus, Danes say Jeg missede bussen (I missed the bus).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **gå glip af** koncerten.
sentence.en: I don't want to miss out on the concert.

at gå hjem.explanation: "At gå hjem" means "to go home", usually on foot: Jeg går hjem nu (I am going home now). By car, say at køre hjem (to drive home). At tage hjem (to head home) works whatever way you travel.

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og vil **gå hjem**.
sentence.en: I am tired and want to go home.

at gå i biografen.explanation: "At gå i biografen" means "to go to the movies". Literally, it is to walk in the cinema, but it is the normal phrase even if you drive. You can also say the shorter at gå i bio (to go to the movies).

forms.en: I have gone to the movies

sentence.da: Vi vil **gå i biografen** i aften.
sentence.en: We want to go to the movies tonight.

at gå i gang med.explanation: "At gå i gang med" means "to get started on", for beginning a task. Med is followed by what you start: Hun gik i gang med maden (She got started on the food). Without it, say Vi er gået i gang (We have started).

forms.da: jeg er gået i gang med

sentence.da: Vi skal **gå i gang med** opgaven nu.
sentence.en: We have to get started on the task now.

at gå i panik.explanation: "At gå i panik" means "to panic", literally "to go into panic": Hun gik i panik, da lyset gik (She panicked when the lights went out). The calm opposite is at bevare roen (to stay calm).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **gå i panik**, for vi har god tid.
sentence.en: Don't panic, because we have plenty of time.

at gå i seng.explanation: "At gå i seng" means "to go to bed": Godnat, jeg går i seng (Good night, I am going to bed). Falling asleep is something different: at falde i søvn (to fall asleep).

sentence.da: Børnene er trætte og skal **gå i seng**.
sentence.en: The children are tired and have to go to bed.

at gå i stykker.explanation: "At gå i stykker" means "to break": Min telefon gik i stykker (My phone broke). It is for something that falls apart or stops working. To break it yourself, use at ødelægge (to destroy): Jeg ødelagde telefonen (I broke the phone).

sentence.da: Den gamle cykel kan nemt **gå i stykker**.
sentence.en: The old bike can easily break.

at gå igennem.explanation: "At gå igennem" means "to go through", passing from one side of a place to the other: Vi gik igennem skoven (We went through the forest). It also means "to go over" something, checking it step by step: Vi går opgaven igennem (We go over the task).

sentence.da: Vi kan **gå igennem** tunnelen til den anden side.
sentence.en: We can go through the tunnel to the other side.

at gå ind.explanation: "At gå ind" means "to go in", walking into a place such as a room or a house. Danish has two little words: ind for going in, and "inde" for being inside: Han er inde i huset (He is inside the house).

sentence.da: Vi skal **gå ind** i huset nu.
sentence.en: We have to go into the house now.

at gå ned.explanation: "At gå ned" means "to go down", moving to a lower place, such as a basement or down a hill. It is also used for the sun: solen går ned means "the sun sets".

sentence.da: Vi skal **gå ned** ad trappen.
sentence.en: We have to walk down the stairs.

at gå op.explanation: "At gå op" means "to go up", moving to a higher place, such as an upper floor or up a hill. It is also used for the sun: solen går op means "the sun rises".

sentence.da: Vi skal **gå op** ad trappen.
sentence.en: We have to walk up the stairs.

at gå på café.explanation: "At gå på café" means "to go to a café". Danish says på café (literally on café) with no en (a), and the same goes for på restaurant (to a restaurant).

forms.en: I have gone to a café

related.en: to go out on the town

sentence.da: Vi vil **gå på café** i dag.
sentence.en: We want to go to a café today.

at gå rundt.explanation: "At gå rundt" means "to walk around", with no fixed goal: Vi gik rundt i byen hele dagen (We walked around town all day). With om it means "around something": Vi gik rundt om søen (We walked around the lake).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **gå rundt** og se på butikkerne.
sentence.en: I would like to walk around and look at the shops.

at gå til eksamen.explanation: "At gå til eksamen" means "to take an exam", sitting a test at school or university. It is for the exam itself, not studying for it: Hun går til eksamen i juni (She takes her exam in June).

sentence.da: Jeg har læst meget, og nu skal jeg **gå til eksamen**.
sentence.en: I have studied a lot, and now I have to take the exam.

at gå tilbage.explanation: "At gå tilbage" means "to go back", returning to where you came from: Jeg går tilbage til hotellet (I walk back to the hotel). It is about going on foot. By car, say at køre tilbage (to drive back).

sentence.da: Nu skal vi **gå tilbage** til stationen.
sentence.en: Now we have to walk back to the station.

at gå ud.explanation: "At gå ud" means "to go out", either to leave a place such as the house, or to go out for the evening, for example to a bar or restaurant: Skal vi gå ud? (Shall we go out?).

sentence.da: Vi vil **gå ud** i haven nu.
sentence.en: We want to go out into the garden now.

at gå ud fra.explanation: "At gå ud fra" means "to assume", taking something as true without checking: Jeg går ud fra, at du har tid (I assume you have time).

sentence.da: Vi må **gå ud fra**, at han kommer.
sentence.en: We have to assume that he is coming.

at gå ud med.explanation: "At gå ud med" means "to go out with", as in dating someone: Hun går ud med Peter (She is going out with Peter). It also means taking something out: Jeg går ud med hunden (I am taking the dog out).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **gå ud med** hende, fordi han kan lide hende.
sentence.en: He would like to go out with her because he likes her.

at gå videre.explanation: "At gå videre" means "to move on", going on to the next thing: Nu går vi videre til næste side (Now we move on to the next page). It also fits life: Hun er gået videre (She has moved on).

sentence.da: Efter pausen skal vi **gå videre** til næste emne.
sentence.en: After the break we move on to the next topic.

at gå væk.explanation: "At gå væk" means "to go away" or "to walk off", leaving a place. As a command, Gå væk! means "Go away!", a blunt order like "Get lost!", so be careful.

sentence.da: Katten vil **gå væk** fra hunden.
sentence.en: The cat wants to go away from the dog.

at gætte.explanation: "At gætte" means "to guess", giving an answer without knowing it for sure. To name your guess, add på: Jeg gætter på Peter (I am guessing Peter). Gæt hvad! means "Guess what!".

sentence.da: Kan du **gætte** min alder?
sentence.en: Can you guess my age?

at gø.explanation: "At gø" means "to bark", and it is used for dogs: Hunden gøede hele natten (The dog barked all night). The present form gør looks exactly like gør from at gøre (to do), so the sentence tells you which one it is.

sentence.da: Hunden må ikke **gø** om natten.
sentence.en: The dog is not allowed to bark at night.

at gøre.explanation: "At gøre" means "to do", as in Hvad gør du? (What are you doing?). It can stand in for an action you do not want to repeat: Jeg læser, og det gør hun også (I am reading, and she does too). For making things, such as food, Danish uses at lave (to make): at lave mad (to cook).

sentence.da: Hvad vil du **gøre** i dag?
sentence.en: What do you want to do today?

at gøre det forbi.explanation: "At gøre det forbi" means "to end it", about a relationship: Han gjorde det forbi med hende (He ended it with her). A common everyday way to say it is at slå op (to break up).

sentence.da: Hun elsker ham ikke mere og vil **gøre det forbi**.
sentence.en: She no longer loves him and wants to end it.

at gøre en forskel.explanation: "At gøre en forskel" means "to make a difference": Din hjælp gør en forskel (Your help makes a difference). To say how big, add a word: at gøre en stor forskel (to make a big difference).

sentence.da: Et smil kan **gøre en forskel** for en ensom person.
sentence.en: A smile can make a difference for a lonely person.

at gøre færdig.explanation: "At gøre færdig" means "to finish" something: Jeg gør opgaven færdig (I am finishing the assignment). To say you are done yourself, use at blive færdig: Jeg bliver færdig klokken fem (I will be done at five).

sentence.da: Lad mig lige **gøre færdig**, og så kommer jeg.
sentence.en: Let me just finish, and then I will come.

at gøre grin med.explanation: "At gøre grin med" means "to make fun of" someone: Hun gør grin med mig (She makes fun of me). The person or thing you laugh at comes after med (with).

sentence.da: Man skal ikke **gøre grin med** andre.
sentence.en: You should not make fun of others.

at gøre klar.explanation: "At gøre klar" means "to get something ready": Jeg gør maden klar (I am getting the food ready). To get yourself ready, add mig: Jeg gør mig klar (I am getting myself ready).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **gøre klar** til festen.
sentence.en: I have to get ready for the party.

at gøre noget ved.explanation: "At gøre noget ved" means "to do something about" a problem: Vi må gøre noget ved støjen (We have to do something about the noise). Said alone, Gør noget! means "Do something!".

sentence.da: Vi må **gøre noget ved** det nu.
sentence.en: We have to do something about it now.

at gøre ondt.explanation: "At gøre ondt" means "to hurt". The part that hurts comes first: Min fod gør ondt (My foot hurts). You can also say Jeg har ondt i foden (I have a pain in the foot).

sentence.da: Min arm kan **gøre ondt** efter faldet.
sentence.en: My arm can hurt after the fall.

at gøre rent.explanation: "At gøre rent" means "to clean" a place. It is built from gøre (to do) and rent (clean), so it literally means to make clean. The place can go in the middle: Jeg gør køkkenet rent (I clean the kitchen).

sentence.da: Vi skal **gøre rent** i huset.
sentence.en: We have to clean the house.

at gøre sit bedste.explanation: "At gøre sit bedste" means "to do one's best". Sit (one's) changes with who does it: Han gør sit bedste (He does his best), Jeg gør mit bedste (I do my best).

sentence.da: Hver elev skal **gøre sit bedste** til prøven.
sentence.en: Each student must do their best for the test.

en gade.explanation: "En gade" means "a street". For a bigger road, for example between towns, use en vej (a road).

sentence.da: Vi går ned ad en **gade** med huse.
sentence.en: We walk down a street with houses.

en gadedør.explanation: "En gadedør" means "a street door", the main door of a building that opens onto the street. It is built from gade (street) and dør (door). Dør also means "dies", as in Fuglen dør (The bird dies).

sentence.da: Huset har en blå **gadedør** ud til gaden.
sentence.en: The house has a blue street door facing the street.

en gadekat.explanation: "En gadekat" means "a stray cat", a cat with no home. It is built from gade (street) and kat (cat). A cat that lives with a family is en huskat (a house cat).

sentence.da: En **gadekat** bor ude og har ingen ejer.
sentence.en: A stray cat lives outside and has no owner.

en gadelygte.explanation: "En gadelygte" means "a streetlight". It is built from gade (street) and lygte (light), and gade also starts en gadekat (a stray cat).

sentence.da: Om natten giver en **gadelygte** lys på gaden.
sentence.en: At night a streetlight gives light on the street.

en gaffel.explanation: "En gaffel" means "a fork", the pointed tool you use to pick up food. It is paired with a knife in the set phrase kniv og gaffel (knife and fork).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser maden med en **gaffel**.
sentence.en: I eat the food with a fork.

en gang.explanation: "En gang" means "a hallway", the passage inside a building that leads to the rooms. The same word also means "a time": to gange (twice).

sentence.da: Der er mange døre i den lange **gang**.
sentence.en: There are many doors in the long hallway.

en gang imellem.explanation: "En gang imellem" means "once in a while", for things that do not happen often. It sounds more rare than tit (often) and less rare than aldrig (never).

forms.da: Jeg ser dem en gang imellem.
forms.en: I see them once in a while.
once in a while in the summer

forms.da: Vi spiser ude en gang imellem.
forms.en: We eat out once in a while.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser pizza **en gang imellem**.
sentence.en: I eat pizza once in a while.

en gang om ugen.explanation: "En gang om ugen" means "once a week". Change the number to say how often: tre gange om ugen (three times a week). Change the last word to change the time: en gang om dagen (once a day).

sentence.da: Jeg træner **en gang om ugen**.
sentence.en: I work out once a week.

en garage.explanation: "En garage" means "a garage", where you park a car.

sentence.da: Vi har en **garage** til bilen.
sentence.en: We have a garage for the car.

en garanti.explanation: "En garanti" means "a warranty", the maker's promise to fix a product. It also means "a guarantee" in general: Jeg giver dig min garanti (I give you my guarantee).

sentence.da: Der er to års **garanti** på computeren.
sentence.en: The computer has a two-year warranty.

en gartner.explanation: "En gartner" means "a gardener", someone who works with plants and flowers as a job. The workplace is et gartneri (a plant nursery).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **gartner** og passer planter i parken.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a gardener and takes care of plants in the park.

en gate.explanation: "En gate" means "a gate" at an airport, where you board your plane. A garden gate is en låge (a gate).

sentence.da: Flyet til Rom går fra **gate** tolv.
sentence.en: The plane to Rome leaves from gate twelve.

en gaveindpakning.explanation: "En gaveindpakning" means "a gift wrapping", the paper and ribbon around a present, or the wrapping service in a shop: Kan jeg få den i gaveindpakning? (Can I get it gift wrapped?)

sentence.da: Butikken tilbyder gratis **gaveindpakning**.
sentence.en: The shop offers free gift wrapping.

en ged.explanation: "En ged" means "a goat", a farm animal with horns. Goat cheese is called gedeost.

sentence.da: En **ged** spiser græs og giver mælk.
sentence.en: A goat eats grass and gives milk.

en genbrugsbutik.explanation: "En genbrugsbutik" means "a secondhand shop", a store that sells clothes and things that other people owned before.

sentence.da: I en **genbrugsbutik** er tøjet brugt og billigt.
sentence.en: In a secondhand shop the clothes are used and cheap.

en genbrugsstation.explanation: "En genbrugsstation" means "a recycling center", where you leave bigger things you no longer need, like old furniture or branches.

sentence.da: Man sorterer sit affald på en **genbrugsstation**.
sentence.en: You sort your waste at a recycling center.

en genre.explanation: "En genre" means "a genre", a type of music, film or book.

sentence.da: Rock er en **genre** inden for musik.
sentence.en: Rock is a genre within music.

en genstand.explanation: "En genstand" means "an object", a physical item you can point to. Everyday speech uses et ting (a thing): Hvad er det for en ting? (What is that thing?). A report says en ukendt genstand (an unidentified item).

sentence.da: Politiet fandt en mærkelig **genstand** i haven.
sentence.en: The police found a strange object in the garden.

en genvej.explanation: "En genvej" means "a shortcut", a quicker way to get somewhere. It is also used on computers: en tastaturgenvej (a keyboard shortcut).

sentence.da: Vi tog en **genvej** og kom hurtigt hjem.
sentence.en: We took a shortcut and got home quickly.

en gift.explanation: "En gift" means "a poison", something that can make you very sick. The same spelling also means "married": Han er gift (He is married).

sentence.da: Slangen har en stærk **gift**.
sentence.en: The snake has a strong poison.

en giraf.explanation: "En giraf" means "a giraffe", the tallest animal on land, found in Africa.

sentence.da: En **giraf** har en meget lang hals.
sentence.en: A giraffe has a very long neck.

en globus.explanation: "En globus" means "a globe", a round model of the Earth. A flat picture of the world is et kort (a map).

sentence.da: På en **globus** ser man hele jorden.
sentence.en: On a globe you see the whole Earth.

en gorilla.explanation: "En gorilla" means "a gorilla", a big, strong animal that lives in the forests of Africa.

sentence.da: Den store **gorilla** spiser blade og frugt.
sentence.en: The big gorilla eats leaves and fruit.

en grad.explanation: "En grad" means "a degree", for temperature, angles and university studies: Vandet fryser ved nul grader (Water freezes at zero degrees). Hun har en grad fra universitetet (She has a degree from the university).

sentence.da: Det er kun én **grad** ude i dag.
sentence.en: It is only one degree outside today.

en grammatik.explanation: "En grammatik" means "a grammar", the system for how words fit together in speech and writing.

sentence.da: Jeg øver reglerne i dansk **grammatik**.
sentence.en: I practice the rules of Danish grammar.

en gravko.explanation: "En gravko" means "an excavator", a big machine that digs holes. The word is built from grave (dig) and ko (cow). Grave also gives en grav (a grave).

sentence.da: En **gravko** graver et stort hul.
sentence.en: An excavator digs a big hole.

en gren.explanation: "En gren" means "a branch", the woody part that grows out sideways from a tree.

sentence.da: Fuglen sidder på en **gren** i træet.
sentence.en: The bird sits on a branch in the tree.

en grill.explanation: "En grill" means "a grill" or "a barbecue", for cooking outside. The matching verb is at grille (to grill): Vi griller pølser (We grill sausages).

sentence.da: Vi laver mad ude på en **grill**.
sentence.en: We cook outside on a grill.

en grillfest.explanation: "En grillfest" means "a barbecue party". It is built from en grill (a grill) and en fest (a party). The verb at grille (to grill) is how you say you are barbecuing: Vi griller i aften (We are barbecuing tonight).

sentence.da: Til en **grillfest** spiser vi pølser og salat.
sentence.en: At a barbecue party we eat sausages and salad.

en gris.explanation: "En gris" means "a pig". Du er en gris! (You are a pig!) is an insult, so keep the word for the animal. Pork is svinekød, built from et svin (a swine), another word for pig.

sentence.da: Jeg ser en lyserød **gris** på gården.
sentence.en: I see a pink pig on the farm.

en grund.explanation: "En grund" means "a reason". Af den grund means "for that reason". It can also mean a plot of land that you build on: Vi køber en grund og bygger et hus (We buy a plot of land and build a house).

sentence.da: Der er ingen **grund** til at være bange.
sentence.en: There is no reason to be afraid.

en gruppe.explanation: "En gruppe" means "a group" of people or things. Danish has no word for "of" here: en gruppe børn (a group of children).

sentence.da: Vi arbejder i en **gruppe** på fire.
sentence.en: We work in a group of four.

en gryde.explanation: "En gryde" means "a pot", for cooking soup, pasta or rice on the stove. For frying you use en pande (a pan) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg koger kartofler i en stor **gryde**.
sentence.en: I boil potatoes in a big pot.

en grydelap.explanation: "En grydelap" means "a pot holder", a thick cloth for holding hot things.

sentence.da: Jeg tager brødet ud af ovnen med en **grydelap**.
sentence.en: I take the bread out of the oven with a pot holder.

en grænse.explanation: "En grænse" means "a border", for example between two countries. It also means a limit: Alt har en grænse (Everything has a limit).

sentence.da: Ved en **grænse** skal du vise dit pas.
sentence.en: At a border you must show your passport.

en græsslåmaskine.explanation: "En græsslåmaskine" means "a lawnmower". It is built from græs (grass), at slå (to mow) and en maskine (a machine). Slå also means to hit, so at slå græs (to mow grass) is literally to hit grass.

sentence.da: Græsset er højt, og jeg henter min **græsslåmaskine**.
sentence.en: The grass is tall, and I am getting my lawnmower.

en grøntsag.explanation: "En grøntsag" means "a vegetable". It is built from grøn (green) and sag (thing), so it is literally a green thing. Sag is a common word for a matter or a case, as in en retssag (a court case).

sentence.da: En gulerod er en **grøntsag**.
sentence.en: A carrot is a vegetable.

en gud.explanation: "En gud" means "a god", one of many gods. For the one God, say Gud without en: Tror du på Gud? (Do you believe in God?).

sentence.da: Thor var en **gud** i gamle dage.
sentence.en: Thor was a god in the old days.

en gudfar.explanation: "En gudfar" means "a godfather", a man chosen as a special adult in a child's life.

sentence.da: Min **gudfar** er min fars bedste ven.
sentence.en: My godfather is my dad's best friend.

en gudmor.explanation: "En gudmor" means "a godmother", a woman chosen as a special adult in a child's life.

sentence.da: Min **gudmor** er min mors bedste veninde.
sentence.en: My godmother is my mom's best friend.

en guide.explanation: "En guide" means "a guide", a person who shows visitors around a place.

sentence.da: Vores **guide** viser os den gamle by.
sentence.en: Our guide shows us the old town.

en guidebog.explanation: "En guidebog" means "a guidebook", a book with sights and tips for a trip. It is built from guide (guide) and bog (book). Guide also means a person who shows tourists around: En guide viser os byen (A guide shows us the town).

sentence.da: Jeg læser en **guidebog** før turen.
sentence.en: I read a guidebook before the trip.

en guitar.explanation: "En guitar" means "a guitar". When you play it, Danish leaves out the: Jeg spiller guitar means "I play the guitar", using at spille (to play).

sentence.da: Min bror spiller **guitar** i et band.
sentence.en: My brother plays guitar in a band.

en guldfisk.explanation: "En guldfisk" means "a goldfish", an orange pet fish that lives in a bowl.

sentence.da: Der svømmer en **guldfisk** rundt i en skål.
sentence.en: A goldfish is swimming around in a bowl.

en gulerod.explanation: "En gulerod" means "a carrot". It is built from gul (yellow) and rod (root), so it is literally a yellow root. The name says yellow, but you describe the color of a carrot as orange (orange).

sentence.da: Kaninen spiser en orange **gulerod**.
sentence.en: The rabbit eats an orange carrot.

en gummistøvle.explanation: "En gummistøvle" means "a rubber boot", the waterproof boot for rain and mud. Most often you say it in pairs: et par gummistøvler (a pair of rubber boots).

sentence.da: Han mistede en **gummistøvle** i mudderet.
sentence.en: He lost a rubber boot in the mud.

en gynge.explanation: "En gynge" means "a swing", the kind at a playground. The action is at gynge (to swing, to rock): Barnet gynger (The child is swinging).

sentence.da: Far skubber mig på en **gynge**.
sentence.en: Dad pushes me on a swing.

en gågade.explanation: "En gågade" means "a pedestrian street", a street with no cars. It is built from gå (walk) and gade (street). Gade also appears in other street words, such as en sidegade (a side street).

sentence.da: Ingen biler må køre i en **gågade**.
sentence.en: Cars may not drive in a pedestrian street.

en gård.explanation: "En gård" means "a farm" and also "a courtyard". In the country it is a farm. In a city, gården is the shared yard behind an apartment building.

sentence.da: Vi besøger en **gård** og ser køer og grise.
sentence.en: We visit a farm and see cows and pigs.

en gårdhave.explanation: "En gårdhave" means "a courtyard garden", a small garden inside a block of buildings. It is built from gård (courtyard) and have (garden). Gård also means a farm: Vi bor på en gård (We live on a farm).

sentence.da: Der er en lille **gårdhave** med blomster bag huset.
sentence.en: There is a small courtyard garden with flowers behind the house.

en gås.explanation: "En gås" means "a goose", a big bird with a long neck that flies in groups. The meat is also eaten: gåsesteg (roast goose).

sentence.da: En **gås** er en stor fugl og bor ved vandet.
sentence.en: A goose is a big bird and lives by the water.

en gåtur.explanation: "En gåtur" means "a walk". It is built from gå (walk) and tur (trip). You say at gå en tur or at tage på gåtur, both meaning "to go for a walk".

sentence.da: Vi tager på **gåtur** i skoven.
sentence.en: We go for a walk in the forest.

en gæst.explanation: "En gæst" means "a guest", for visitors in your home and also for hotel guests. Vi får gæster means "We are having guests".

sentence.da: Vi laver mad til vores **gæst**.
sentence.en: We cook for our guest.

en gætteleg.explanation: "En gætteleg" means "a guessing game". It is built from at gætte (to guess) and leg (game). Leg also gives at lege (to play): Børnene leger udenfor (The children are playing outside).

sentence.da: I en **gætteleg** skal du gætte svaret.
sentence.en: In a guessing game, you have to guess the answer.

et gadekryds.explanation: "Et gadekryds" means "an intersection", where two streets cross. It is built from en gade (a street) and et kryds (a cross). Kryds also means a cross mark: Sæt et kryds her (Put a cross here).

sentence.da: Drej til højre ved næste **gadekryds**.
sentence.en: Turn right at the next intersection.

et galleri.explanation: "Et galleri" means "a gallery", a place that shows art, often for sale.

sentence.da: Vi ser på kunst i et lille **galleri**.
sentence.en: We look at art in a small gallery.

et gardin.explanation: "Et gardin" means "a curtain", hung at a window. To close it, say trække for (draw): Hun trækker gardinerne for (She draws the curtains).

sentence.da: Et **gardin** hænger foran vinduet og holder lyset ude.
sentence.en: A curtain hangs in front of the window and keeps the light out.

et gavekort.explanation: "Et gavekort" means "a gift card", a card with money on it that you give as a present. It is made of en gave (a gift) and et kort (a card).

sentence.da: Med et **gavekort** kan man købe ting.
sentence.en: With a gift card you can buy things.

et gear.explanation: "Et gear" means "a gear", on a car or a bike: Jeg kører i andet gear (I am driving in second gear).

sentence.da: Jeg skifter **gear**, når vejen går opad.
sentence.en: I shift gears when the road goes uphill.

et geni.explanation: "Et geni" means "a genius", a person with a brilliant mind. To say what someone is brilliant at, use i or til: Hun er et geni i matematik (She is a genius at math).

sentence.da: Min bror er et **geni** til matematik.
sentence.en: My brother is a genius at math.

et gennemsnit.explanation: "Et gennemsnit" means "an average", the middle value of a group of numbers. With i, it means "on average": i gennemsnit.

sentence.da: Jeg sover syv timer i **gennemsnit**.
sentence.en: I sleep seven hours on average.

et glas.explanation: "Et glas" means "a glass", both the material and a drinking glass. Danish has no word for "of" here: et glas vand is a glass of water, and "et glas vin" is a glass of wine.

sentence.da: Man drikker vand af et **glas**.
sentence.en: You drink water from a glass.

et gram.explanation: "Et gram" means "a gram", a unit of weight used for small amounts, such as flour or spices.

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge to hundrede **gram** mel.
sentence.en: I need two hundred grams of flour.

et grin.explanation: "Et grin" means "a laugh". A smile is et smil (a smile).

sentence.da: Vi fik et godt **grin** sammen i går.
sentence.en: We had a good laugh together yesterday.

et gudbarn.explanation: "Et gudbarn" means "a godchild", a child you are a godparent to.

sentence.da: Mit **gudbarn** fylder fem år i dag.
sentence.en: My godchild turns five today.

et gulv.explanation: "Et gulv" means "a floor", the surface you walk on in a room. For a level of a building, such as the second floor, Danes say en etage.

sentence.da: Et **gulv** er lavet af træ eller sten.
sentence.en: A floor is made of wood or stone.

et gulvtæppe.explanation: "Et gulvtæppe" means "a carpet". Gulv (floor) shows that it lies on the floor, since et tæppe alone can also be a blanket.

sentence.da: Vi har et blødt **gulvtæppe** i stuen.
sentence.en: We have a soft carpet in the living room.

et gymnasium.explanation: "Et gymnasium" means "a high school", the three years at about age 16 to 19 that prepare you for further study: Min datter går på gymnasiet (My daughter goes to high school). For a sports hall, say en idrætshal (a sports hall).

sentence.da: Efter folkeskolen går mange unge på et **gymnasium**.
sentence.en: After primary school, many young people go to a gymnasium.

et gæsteværelse.explanation: "Et gæsteværelse" means "a guest room", the room in your home for people who sleep over. It is built from gæst (guest) and værelse (room).

sentence.da: Du kan sove i vores **gæsteværelse**.
sentence.en: You can sleep in our guest room.

gal.explanation: "Gal" means "crazy", for a person or idea that is mad or foolish. It also means "wrong" when something goes badly: Noget gik galt (Something went wrong), Det er galt (That is wrong).

sentence.da: Er du helt **gal**? Det er alt for farligt!
sentence.en: Are you completely crazy? That is far too dangerous!

galt.explanation: "Galt" means "wrong" and "bad": Jeg gjorde noget galt (I did something wrong). Before an en-word you use gal, which also means "crazy": en gal idé (a crazy idea).

sentence.da: Noget er **galt** med min computer.
sentence.en: Something is wrong with my computer.

gammel.explanation: "Gammel" means "old", for things (en gammel bil, an old car) and for a person's age. To ask age, you say Hvor gammel er du? (How old are you?) and answer Jeg er tredive år gammel (I am thirty years old).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er 90 år og meget **gammel**.
sentence.en: My grandfather is 90 and very old.

gammeldags.explanation: "Gammeldags" means "old-fashioned". Danish uses this one form with en-words, et-words and plurals. The opposite is moderne (modern).

sentence.da: Min mormor har et **gammeldags** køkken.
sentence.en: My grandmother has an old-fashioned kitchen.

gang.explanation: "Gang" means "a time" in the sense of an occasion: en gang means "once" and "to gange" means "twice". It can also mean a hallway in a house. Do not mix it up with tid (time in general). Hvor mange gange? means "How many times?".

sentence.da: Jeg har været i Paris en **gang**.
sentence.en: I have been to Paris once.

ganske.explanation: "Ganske" means "quite" or "fairly". It is weaker than meget (very), so ganske kold (quite cold) is less cold than meget kold (very cold).

sentence.da: Maden var **ganske** god, men lidt dyr.
sentence.en: The food was quite good, but a little expensive.

gavepapir.explanation: "Gavepapir" means "wrapping paper", the paper you wrap presents in. It is built from gave (present) and papir (paper). It has no plural, so you count it in rolls.

sentence.da: Jeg pakker gaven ind i rødt **gavepapir**.
sentence.en: I wrap the gift in red wrapping paper.

generelt.explanation: "Generelt" means "generally" and talks about the big picture, not every case. One specific day can be different: Generelt er bussen til tiden, men i dag var den sen (Generally the bus is on time, but today it was late).

sentence.da: **Generelt** er det varmt i juli, men ikke altid.
sentence.en: Generally it is warm in July, but not always.

genert.explanation: "Genert" means "shy", nervous around other people: Han er genert over for fremmede (He is shy around strangers).

sentence.da: Jeg er lidt **genert**, når jeg møder nye folk.
sentence.en: I am a bit shy when I meet new people.

generøs.explanation: "Generøs" means "generous" and describes someone who gives freely: Hun er generøs med sin tid (She is generous with her time). The opposite is nærig (stingy).

sentence.da: Han er **generøs** og giver gerne penge væk.
sentence.en: He is generous and gladly gives money away.

genial.explanation: "Genial" means "brilliant", extremely clever. You can use it for an idea or for a person: Hun er genial (She is brilliant).

sentence.da: Det er en **genial** idé, og den virker.
sentence.en: It is a brilliant idea, and it works.

gennem.explanation: "Gennem" means "through": Vi kører gennem tunnelen (We drive through the tunnel). With time, it means "throughout": Jeg har boet her gennem mange år (I have lived here for many years).

sentence.da: Vi går **gennem** parken hjem.
sentence.en: We walk home through the park.

geografi.explanation: "Geografi" means "geography", the study of countries and landscapes at school.

sentence.da: Vi lærer om lande og floder i **geografi**.
sentence.en: We learn about countries and rivers in geography.

gerne.explanation: "Gerne" means "gladly" and makes you sound polite. Compare Jeg vil have kaffe (I want coffee), which sounds blunt, with Jeg vil gerne have kaffe (I would like coffee). On its own it is a friendly yes: Skal vi gå? - Ja, gerne! (Shall we go? - Yes, gladly!).

forms.en: I am happy to do that.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **gerne** have en kop te.
sentence.en: I would like a cup of tea.

gift.explanation: "Gift" means "married". Jeg er gift means "I am married", and you add med (with) for the partner: gift med Peter (married to Peter). Careful: gift is also the word for poison, so context shows which one is meant.

sentence.da: Jeg er **gift** med Anna.
sentence.en: I am married to Anna.

gin.explanation: "Gin" means "gin", a clear strong drink with a juniper taste. Without en it is the drink in general, and with en it is one serving: Jeg kan ikke lide gin (I don't like gin), but Hun drikker en gin (She is drinking a gin).

sentence.da: Hun bestiller en **gin** og tonic i baren.
sentence.en: She orders a gin and tonic at the bar.

glad.explanation: "Glad" means "happy", the everyday word for feeling pleased or cheerful. Add for (for) to say what makes you happy: Jeg er glad for gaven (I am happy about the gift).

sentence.da: Drengen smiler og er så **glad**.
sentence.en: The boy smiles and is so happy.

glad for.explanation: "Glad for" means "fond of" or "happy with" something or someone. It is milder than elske (to love), so it is a warm way to say you care about someone without saying "I love you".

forms.da: Hun er glad for sin bil.
forms.en: She is happy with her car.

sentence.da: Jeg er meget **glad for** min lejlighed.
sentence.en: I am very happy with my apartment.

glat.explanation: "Glat" means "smooth", with no bumps or roughness. It also means "slippery", for things like ice or a wet road.

sentence.da: Pas på, gulvet er **glat**.
sentence.en: Be careful, the floor is slippery.

glimrende.explanation: "Glimrende" means "excellent" and is stronger than god (good).

sentence.da: Du har lavet et **glimrende** stykke arbejde.
sentence.en: You have done an excellent piece of work.

gluten.explanation: "Gluten" means "gluten", the protein in many types of grain. To say without it, add fri: glutenfri (gluten-free).

sentence.da: Der er **gluten** i hvedebrød.
sentence.en: There is gluten in wheat bread.

glutenfri.explanation: "Glutenfri" means "gluten-free", made without gluten. It is built from gluten and fri (free). Fri works the same in many words: alkoholfri (alcohol-free).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser kun **glutenfri** pasta.
sentence.en: I only eat gluten-free pasta.

glæde.explanation: "Glæde" means "joy". With sig, at glæde sig means to look forward: Jeg glæder mig til ferien (I am looking forward to the vacation).

sentence.da: Hendes ansigt lyste af **glæde**.
sentence.en: Her face lit up with joy.

glædelig jul.explanation: "Glædelig jul" means "merry Christmas". Glædelig means "merry" and jul means "Christmas". A reply is i lige måde (same to you), and you can add og godt nytår (and happy New Year).

forms.en: Merry Christmas and happy New Year.

sentence.da: Vi har gaver og et juletræ. **Glædelig jul**!
sentence.en: We have presents and a Christmas tree. Merry Christmas!

god.explanation: "God" means "good", and it appears in greetings like god morgen (good morning) and godt nytår (happy New Year). To say something goes well, use godt: Det går godt (It is going well).

sentence.da: Han hjælper altid. Han er en **god** ven.
sentence.en: He always helps. He is a good friend.

god appetit.explanation: "God appetit" means "enjoy your meal", like bon appétit, and is said just before eating. Danes also say velbekomme (enjoy / you are welcome), often when the food is served or after the meal. A reply is i lige måde (same to you) or tak (thanks).

sentence.da: Maden er klar. **God appetit**!
sentence.en: The food is ready. Enjoy your meal!

god bedring.explanation: "God bedring" means "get well soon" and is said to someone who is sick or hurt. Bedring means "improvement", so you are wishing them a good recovery.

forms.en: Get well soon with your cold.

sentence.da: Du er syg? **God bedring**!
sentence.en: Are you sick? Get well soon!

god fornøjelse.explanation: "God fornøjelse" means "enjoy", said to someone who is about to see or do something fun. Do not use it for a meal; say velbekomme or god appetit (both: enjoy your meal).

sentence.da: Vi skal i teatret. **God fornøjelse**!
sentence.en: We are going to the theater. Enjoy!

god påske.explanation: "God påske" means "happy Easter" and is said before and during the Easter holiday. A reply is i lige måde (same to you).

sentence.da: Vi ses efter ferien. **God påske**!
sentence.en: See you after the holiday. Happy Easter!

god til.explanation: "God til" means "good at" something. After til (to), you can put a thing (god til matematik, good at math) or an action with at (god til at synge, good at singing).

forms.da: Jeg er god til at lave mad.
Han er ikke god til sport.
forms.en: He is not good at sports.

sentence.da: Han er **god til** at spille fodbold.
sentence.en: He is good at playing soccer.

god tur.explanation: "God tur" means "have a good trip" and is said to anyone setting off, whether by car, train, bike or plane. For a longer journey, you can say god rejse (have a good journey). A reply is tak (thanks).

forms.en: Have a good trip to Copenhagen.

sentence.da: Vi tager af sted nu. — **God tur**!
sentence.en: We are leaving now. — Have a good trip!

god weekend.explanation: "God weekend" means "have a good weekend". It is said when parting before the weekend. A reply is i lige måde (same to you). On Monday, people ask Havde du en god weekend? (Did you have a good weekend?).

forms.en: Have a good weekend, all of you.

sentence.da: Vi ses på mandag. **God weekend**!
sentence.en: See you on Monday. Have a good weekend!

godaften.explanation: "Godaften" means "good evening". You say it when you meet someone in the evening. Do not use it when you go to bed; then you say godnat (good night).

sentence.da: Det er aften. **Godaften**, Peter!
sentence.en: It is evening. Good evening, Peter!

goddag.explanation: "Goddag" means "good day", a polite, slightly formal way to say hello at any time of day. Friends usually say hej (hi) instead. You answer goddag with goddag back.

sentence.da: **Goddag**, jeg hedder Peter.
sentence.en: Hello, my name is Peter.

godmorgen.explanation: "Godmorgen" means "good morning", said until late morning. For later in the day, you switch to goddag (good day).

sentence.da: **Godmorgen**! Har du sovet godt?
sentence.en: Good morning! Did you sleep well?

godnat.explanation: "Godnat" means "good night" and is said when you or someone else is going to bed, or when you part late in the evening. It is not a greeting for meeting someone: for that use godaften (good evening).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og går i seng. **Godnat**!
sentence.en: I am tired and going to bed. Good night!

godt nytår.explanation: "Godt nytår" means "happy New Year". Note the spelling: godt nytår, not god nytår. Nytår means "New Year" and "godt" means "good". A reply is i lige måde (same to you).

forms.en: Happy New Year to you all.

sentence.da: Det er midnat. **Godt nytår**!
sentence.en: It is midnight. Happy New Year!

golf.explanation: "Golf" means "golf", the sport where you hit a small ball into holes with clubs.

sentence.da: Jeg spiller **golf** på en grøn bane.
sentence.en: I play golf on a green course.

grader.explanation: "Grader" means "degrees", and it is used for temperature: Det er fem grader means "It is five degrees". For below zero, Danes say minus: Det er minus to grader (It is minus two degrees).

sentence.da: Der er kun fem **grader** udenfor.
sentence.en: It is only five degrees outside.

gratis.explanation: "Gratis" means "free", as in costing no money: Kaffen er gratis (The coffee is free). Do not mix it up with fri, which means free time or freedom: Jeg har fri i dag (I have the day off today).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke betale. Det er **gratis**.
sentence.en: You do not have to pay. It is free.

grillkul.explanation: "Grillkul" means "charcoal", the fuel for a barbecue. It is built from grill (barbecue) and kul (coal). The same grill is in at grille (to barbecue).

sentence.da: Vi lægger **grillkul** i grillen og tænder det.
sentence.en: We put charcoal in the grill and light it.

grim.explanation: "Grim" means "ugly", for people, buildings or things. It can also mean unpleasant: grimt vejr (nasty weather) and et grimt ord (a nasty word). Saying Du er grim (You are ugly) to a person is very rude.

sentence.da: Bygningen er **grim** og ikke smuk.
sentence.en: The building is ugly and not beautiful.

grå.explanation: "Grå" means "gray". It is also used for weather: en grå dag (a gray day) is a dull, cloudy day.

sentence.da: Himlen er **grå** og ikke blå.
sentence.en: The sky is gray and not blue.

gråvejr.explanation: "Gråvejr" means "gray weather": dull, overcast weather with a gray sky, but not necessarily rain. It is made from grå (gray) and vejr (weather).

sentence.da: Der er **gråvejr** og grå himmel.
sentence.en: It is gray weather with a gray sky.

grækenland.explanation: "Grækenland" means "Greece". It is built from græker (a Greek person) and land (country). Land ends many country names: Tyskland (Germany) and Finland (Finland).

sentence.da: Athen er en by i **Grækenland**.
sentence.en: Athens is a city in Greece.

græs.explanation: "Græs" means "grass". To mow the lawn, Danes say at slå græs (literally to hit grass).

sentence.da: Koen æder **græs** på marken.
sentence.en: The cow eats grass in the field.

græsk.explanation: "Græsk" means "Greek", for the language and for anything from that country.

sentence.da: Hun er fra Grækenland og taler **græsk**.
sentence.en: She is from Greece and speaks Greek.

grød.explanation: "En grød" means "a porridge". It is normally not counted, so you do not say two porridges. Add the grain in front to name the kind: havregrød (oat porridge).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser varm **grød** med mælk til morgenmad.
sentence.en: I eat warm porridge with milk for breakfast.

grøn.explanation: "Grøn" means "green". It also means eco-friendly: grøn energi means "green energy". Vegetables are grøntsager, literally green things.

sentence.da: Bilen er **grøn** som græs.
sentence.en: The car is green like grass.

grønland.explanation: "Grønland" means "Greenland". It is built from grøn (green) and land (country), so literally green land. Land ends many country names: Tyskland (Germany) and Finland (Finland).

sentence.da: **Grønland** er en stor ø med is.
sentence.en: Greenland is a big island with ice.

grøntsager.explanation: "Grøntsager" means "vegetables". In shops, the section is often labeled frugt og grønt (fruit and vegetables).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser gulerødder og andre **grøntsager**.
sentence.en: I eat carrots and other vegetables.

sentence.da: Solen er **gul** og himlen blå.
sentence.en: The sun is yellow and the sky is blue.

guld.explanation: "Guld" means "gold", the metal. It can also mean something very precious: Du er guld værd (literally You are worth gold) means "You are worth your weight in gold".

sentence.da: Ringen er lavet af **guld**.
sentence.en: The ring is made of gold.

gummi.explanation: "Gummi" means "rubber", the soft material that stretches and keeps water out. It also starts the word for chewy candy: gummibjørne (gummy bears).

sentence.da: Støvler af **gummi** holder fødderne tørre.
sentence.en: Boots made of rubber keep your feet dry.

gylden.explanation: "Gylden" means "golden" and describes the color or the look of gold. For something made of real gold, use guld: en guldring (a gold ring).

sentence.da: Solen var **gylden** over havet.
sentence.en: The sun was golden over the sea.

gymnastik.explanation: "Gymnastik" means "gymnastics", the sport with jumps, rolls and balance work. It also means simple exercises for your body: Jeg laver gymnastik hver morgen (I do exercises every morning).

sentence.da: Børnene går til **gymnastik** to gange om ugen.
sentence.en: The children go to gymnastics twice a week.

gær.explanation: "Gær" means "yeast", the ingredient that makes bread rise.

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **gær**, når jeg bager brød.
sentence.en: I use yeast when I bake bread.

gør det selv.explanation: "Gør det selv" means "do it yourself". It is made of gør (do), det (it) and selv (yourself). Selv stays the same for every person: Hun gør det selv (She does it herself).

sentence.da: Jeg hjælper dig ikke. **Gør det selv**!
sentence.en: I will not help you. Do it yourself!
